summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted to the bariatric surgery service after outpatient gastrostomy tube removal for abdominal pain/tenderness at the tube site and recurrent symptomatic hypoglycemia during transit, requiring oral and IV dextrose. During hospitalization she received IV fluids, glucose monitoring with dextrose as needed, nausea control with ondansetron/promethazine, and acid suppression with PPI; she developed persistent burping without other sequelae, and abdominal radiographs showed no free air or obstruction. Metabolic labs were monitored and repleted as needed, and her diet was advanced gradually from bariatric stage 1 to stage 4 with emphasis on frequent tolerated snacks to prevent hypoglycemia; outpatient follow-up was arranged for further evaluation of post-bypass hypoglycemia/nonabsorption. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with wound care, diet, glucose-check instructions, and medication guidance (including pantoprazole and avoidance of NSAIDs).
problems: Need for prophylactic vaccination and inoculation against influenza
